issues.legal_issue: A consolidation notification covering land in dispute abates the entire pending civil proceeding, including an appeal challenging a preliminary decree.
material_facts: A civil suit sought determination of rights and shares in land that fell within the consolidation scheme.
A preliminary decree dismissing the suit was challenged in a pending title appeal when a consolidation notification covering the area had been issued.

An application seeking abatement under the consolidation law was filed, but the appellate court treated the matter as abated for non-substitution of a deceased respondent rather than deciding the statutory abatement issue.
issues.conclusion: The suit and the appeal abated in their entirety, and the civil proceeding from its commencement came to a naught.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 3 and 4(c) of the Bihar Consolidation of Holdings and Prevention of Fragmentation Act, 1956 provide for abatement of pending proceedings concerning rights or interests in land brought within consolidation, so that consolidation authorities can adjudicate those claims without impediment. Statutory abatement under this scheme differs from abatement under the Code of Civil Procedure: it nullifies the civil proceeding as a whole, not merely the pending appeal. The Court applied Ram Adhar Singh v. Ramroop Singh, Chattar Singh v. Thakur Prasad Singh, Satyanarayan Prasad Sah v. State of Bihar, and Mst. Bibi Rahmani Khatoon v. Harkoo Gope. It rejected the contrary readings in Raja Mahto v. Mangal Mahto and Dr. Jagdish Prasad v. Sardar Satya Narain Singh. The case differed from the final-decree situation discussed in Srinibas Jena, where the preliminary decree had already become final and was not under challenge.

predicates.land_rights_claim_is_within_consolidatio: The pending claim concerns rights or interests in land that consolidation authorities can adjudicate.

issues.definition: When a consolidation notification covers land involved in a pending civil land-rights claim, including an appeal from a preliminary decree, the entire civil proceeding abates.

issues.legal_issue: Findings made in a civil proceeding that has abated under the consolidation scheme cannot be relied on by consolidation authorities to decide the land-rights claim.
material_facts: The civil suit and the appeal concerned the status of a claimant and the parties’ respective rights in disputed land.
The civil proceeding abated after the land was brought within the consolidation scheme.
The consolidation authorities relied on findings recorded in the civil proceeding when deciding the parties’ competing claims.
issues.conclusion: The civil court’s findings became extinct with the abated proceeding and could not be relied on; the matter had to be decided on the material before the consolidation authorities.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 4(c) of the Bihar Consolidation of Holdings and Prevention of Fragmentation Act, 1956, statutory abatement causes the civil proceeding from its commencement to come to a naught, leaving the consolidation authorities to adjudicate the claims under the Act. Satyanarayan Prasad Sah v. State of Bihar and Mst. Bibi Rahmani Khatoon v. Harkoo Gope explain that abatement removes the civil proceedings and their decisions from the consolidation adjudication; the authorities are not to be impeded by those decisions. The Court also relied on Ram Adhar Singh v. Ramroop Singh and Chattar Singh v. Thakur Prasad Singh concerning the effect of statutory abatement.
